note: Outside the stated ICP on every criterion, and the clearest demonstration in this batch that the stated ICP is not functioning as a screen. Successful fails on the present tense: an impressive past — resort hotel business in Hawaii, scuba instructor, college wrestler — but he is not working, is a full-time carer for a father with dementia, and lives on disability and social security. Income fails absolutely: about $2,000 a month fixed, roughly $400 liquid, medical bills outstanding and $2,000 already committed elsewhere. Neglected health fails in the opposite direction to the usual: this is not a neglected area, it is an acute crisis — stage five kidney failure, haemodialysis three times a week, an indwelling catheter and post-treatment cognitive impairment. Good to great fails because this is rescue in the most literal sense; he describes it as a prescription rather than an ambition. Not deconditioned fails on the substance if not on the letter — he is emphatically not gym-averse, which is the exclusion as worded, but he currently does no training at all and is losing muscle mass, so treating the exclusion as satisfied would be reading the words against their purpose. The finding for the rollup is not that the rep called an out-of-ICP prospect; it is that nothing in the qualification chain stopped this call happening. The setter passed him through with notes about a fear of death and an incoming crypto payment, and the ICP as written contains no clinical criterion, no exclusion for active treatment, and nothing that would have caught a dialysis patient before a closer spent an hour selling him loaded ballistic training.
